summary:
It's an interactive educational adventure game on Roblox that turns space exploration into an exciting mission where players learn, explore, and make decisions that matter.
Set in 2045, the story follows a Saudi astronaut crew investigating a mysterious signal from Outpost 72. Guided by NAJM, their robotic companion, players explore the station, restore critical systems, manage oxygen and power, and overcome survival challenges. Along the way, they must collect three hidden messages, solve interconnected puzzles, and uncover the mystery behind the lost transmission.

Inspired by NASA's scientific resources, the game brings real space engineering challenges to life. Players learn to balance competing survival needs, make trade-offs between limited resources, and experience how their decisions affect the success or failure of a space mission.
What makes SADEEM different is how it combines science with storytelling, interactive puzzles, bilingual support, and cooperative multiplayer for up to four players. Instead of simply reading about space, young learners experience its challenges, work together, and discover solutions through gameplay.
Our goal is to make space science fun, accessible, and meaningful, inspiring the next generation of explorers, scientists, and engineers.

SADEEM | OUTPOST 72 — The Lost Message

Challenge: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

We didn't want children to simply learn about space survival. We wanted them to experience the decisions that make survival possible.

The Mission

The year is 2045. A Saudi astronaut crew receives a mysterious transmission from an abandoned space outpost.

Their mission is to investigate the signal, restore the station's essential systems, and determine whether humans could survive in its environment.

Guided by NAJM, their robotic companion, players travel between the Moon and Mars, investigate scientific evidence, recover hidden messages, and operate a space outpost under challenging conditions.

The mission combines a fictional story with educational activities based on NASA research.

1. How It Works

The game is a 3D educational adventure developed in Roblox Studio for children aged 7–12. Players become junior astronauts responsible for exploring, repairing, and operating space research stations.

The gameplay follows a connected mission divided into several stages.

Stage 1 — Mission Briefing and Astronaut Training

The adventure begins at Saudi Mission Control on Earth.

Players meet the mission commander, receive their objectives, complete a basic equipment-repair tutorial, and prepare their astronaut suits.

They then select their first destination:

  • The Moon: Explore lunar terrain, sunlight conditions, gravity, and possible water ice.
  • Mars: Investigate atmospheric conditions, dust, radiation, and resources needed for human survival.

The selected destination determines the first environment players investigate. Both destinations form part of the complete mission.

Stage 2 — Space Travel and Landing

After boarding the spacecraft, players activate its power systems, set the navigation course, and initiate the landing sequence.

Educational information introduces differences between lunar and Martian travel, including distance, gravity, and communication delays.

The stage also introduces how landing requirements differ between the Moon, which has almost no atmosphere, and Mars, which has a very thin atmosphere.

Stage 3 — Restoring Outpost 72

Upon arrival, players discover that the abandoned station is not fully operational.

Before beginning scientific exploration, they must restore three critical systems:

  1. Power: Restart the backup generator to restore electricity.
  2. Oxygen: Reactivate the system that supports breathable air.
  3. Communications: Repair the communication link.

After restoring these systems, players activate NAJM, who introduces the next objectives and helps guide the mission.

This stage demonstrates the dependency between essential outpost systems. Without sufficient power, other operations cannot function normally.

Stage 4 — Planetary Exploration and Scientific Missions

Players leave the station to explore their selected environment. The scientific tasks differ depending on the destination.

On the Moon:

  • Investigate sunlight exposure near the lunar south pole.
  • Compare crater rims, open plains, and permanently shadowed areas.
  • Select a location for solar panels based on available sunlight.
  • Collect lunar samples and explore information from NASA's Apollo missions.
  • Investigate a shadowed crater using findings from NASA's LCROSS mission.

The solar-panel decision affects the amount of power available during the survival simulation.

On Mars:

  • Examine historical atmospheric and weather measurements from NASA's InSight mission.
  • Study temperature, wind, and atmospheric pressure.
  • Choose a solar-panel location based on sunlight, terrain, and dust exposure.
  • Collect surface samples and learn about NASA's rover missions.
  • Complete an oxygen-production puzzle based on NASA's MOXIE experiment.
  • Investigate radiation protection using research from Curiosity's RAD instrument.

These activities connect scientific observations to gameplay decisions. For example, selecting a poorly illuminated location reduces solar power generation, making resource management more difficult later.

Stage 5 — The Lost Message and Scientific Puzzles

The mystery is explored through two connected activities: recovering the hidden message and collecting scientific mission files.

Players locate three hidden key chips:

  • Key Chip 1: Found during planetary exploration.
  • Key Chip 2: Recovered from communication equipment.
  • Key Chip 3: Located within the station's laboratory.

Each chip reveals part of a symbolic cipher. Players combine the recovered information to decode a message from a previous expedition.

The decoded message directs the crew toward the other planetary destination.

Alongside the storyline, players discover three scientific mission files containing real NASA findings:

Mission File

NASA Reference

Scientific Information

01 — Lunar Ice

LCROSS

Evidence of lunar water ice discovered in 2009

02 — Oxygen

MOXIE

Production of 122 grams of oxygen on Mars

03 — Radiation

Curiosity RAD

Reported surface radiation measurements

Each file contains a numerical code derived from its scientific reference. Players use the three codes in the correct order to complete the final transmitter puzzle.

The game distinguishes these scientific findings from the fictional mystery.

Stage 6 — The 72-Hour Survival Challenge

After restoring the station and completing the investigation, players begin a 72-hour simulated survival challenge.

The objective is to keep the outpost operational while managing limited resources and responding to environmental hazards.

Players monitor several interconnected indicators:

  • Power: Electricity generated and consumed by the station.
  • Oxygen: Supply available to support the crew.
  • Food: Resources needed throughout the mission.
  • Radiation Shield: Protection against hazardous radiation.
  • Base Integrity: Condition of the outpost's structure and equipment.
  • Crew Health: The crew's overall condition.

Power is especially important because multiple systems depend on it.

For example, operating the oxygen-production system at a higher level increases oxygen generation but also consumes more electricity. Greenhouse operations and radiation protection introduce additional energy demands.

Players interact with several stations:

  • Power Station: Manage solar generation, clean panels, and repair equipment.
  • Oxygen Station: Adjust oxygen production based on available power.
  • Greenhouse: Balance food production against energy consumption.
  • Radiation Shelter: Manage shielding and crew protection.
  • Communications Station: Maintain communication systems.
  • Rover Station: Support resource recovery and mission operations.

The challenge also introduces emergencies, including dust storms, radiation events, oxygen-system problems, and generator failures.

Players must select how to respond. Their decisions affect available resources and may create additional challenges later.

For example, protecting solar panels during a dust storm can help prevent equipment damage, while activating radiation protection consumes power that could otherwise support other systems.

The simulation demonstrates that maintaining a space habitat requires balancing several connected systems rather than maximizing one resource.

Stage 7 — Mission Report and Second Destination

After the survival challenge, players receive a mission report summarizing their performance, resource management, and survival outcome.

They can then continue to the second destination, where different environmental conditions introduce new engineering considerations.

This allows players to compare the challenges of operating a base on the Moon and Mars.

Stage 8 — Final Mission Report

After completing both destinations, players use the recovered scientific codes to operate the final transmitter.

The game concludes with a report comparing mission outcomes and environmental conditions, including gravity, atmospheric characteristics, temperature, communication delays, and resource challenges.

The objective is not simply to finish the story, but to understand how different environments influence the decisions required for human survival.

2. How We Used NASA Data

NASA resources support the game's scientific tasks, environmental conditions, and educational activities.

Rather than displaying scientific information only as text, SADEEM connects selected NASA findings to interactive decisions.

NASA InSight — Martian Weather

Historical weather records from NASA's InSight lander are included in the simulation, covering temperature, wind, and atmospheric pressure.

For example, the game includes measurements from sols 675–681 in October 2020.

These records are used to represent Martian environmental conditions. Temperature influences simulated heating requirements, while wind conditions contribute to dust accumulation on solar panels.

LRO / LOLA and Diviner — Lunar Exploration

NASA's lunar research supports the Moon's terrain, illumination, and temperature-related activities.

Players compare locations with different sunlight exposure and select a site for their solar array.

The choice affects the station's energy generation during the survival challenge.

Diviner temperature findings also help explain the extreme thermal conditions on the lunar surface.

NASA LCROSS — Lunar Water Ice

NASA's LCROSS findings are incorporated into a lunar exploration activity involving permanently shadowed craters.

Players investigate evidence of water ice and recover scientific information connected to the final mission puzzle.

NASA MOXIE — Oxygen Production

The Mars oxygen-production puzzle is based on NASA's MOXIE experiment aboard the Perseverance rover.

Players identify carbon dioxide as the gas used by MOXIE to produce oxygen, connecting the scientific finding to an interactive station task.

Curiosity RAD — Radiation Protection

NASA's Curiosity radiation measurements support educational content about radiation exposure on Mars.

Players encounter a radiation-related puzzle and must consider protective systems during the survival challenge.

NASA DONKI — Space Weather Hazards

Archived space-weather event records provide scientific context for the game's solar radiation hazard scenarios.

These events are used as educational references, not as real-time predictions of conditions on the Moon or Mars.

NASA JPL Horizons and Planetary Fact Sheets

Planetary positioning data supports the game's educational sky representation.

NASA planetary facts are also used in the observatory and gravity-related activities, allowing players to explore differences in planetary size, distance, and gravitational conditions.

NASA Apollo and Mars Rover Archives

The in-game archive introduces historical lunar exploration and robotic missions, including Apollo, Perseverance, Curiosity, Spirit, and Opportunity.

Players can explore this information to understand how past missions contributed to current knowledge of the Moon and Mars.

Scientific Accuracy

NASA research and archived scientific measurements provide educational references, while the fictional storyline and gameplay systems are designed for younger learners.

The resource values, environmental effects, and survival challenge use simplified simulations rather than actual NASA engineering measurements. The game does not require live NASA data connections.

Detailed scientific sources and their integration status are provided in our separate NASA Data and Sources documentation.

3. What Makes SADEEM Different?

We turned space engineering into an adventure, not a lecture.

SADEEM combines scientific exploration, resource management, and mystery-solving within one connected story.

Its main features include:

  • Mission-Based Learning: Scientific activities are connected to specific mission objectives.
  • Engineering Trade-offs: Decisions about power, oxygen, food, and protection influence other systems.
  • NASA-Based Activities: Historical research becomes part of exploration tasks and educational puzzles.
  • Connected Storyline: Three hidden key chips lead to a decoded message and the next destination.
  • Interactive Companion: NAJM provides guidance, instructions, and mission support.
  • Two Destinations: Players experience different challenges on the Moon and Mars.
  • Cooperative Multiplayer: Up to four players can work together on a shared mission.
  • Bilingual Support: Arabic and English interfaces make the experience more accessible.

Why Roblox?

We selected Roblox because it provides an accessible 3D environment for exploration, interaction, and cooperative gameplay.

It also allows children to experience educational content through a platform familiar to many young players.

4. Development and Technologies

SADEEM was built from scratch during NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, progressing from an initial concept to a playable Roblox experience within the hackathon period.

The team worked on research, programming, storyline development, level design, user interfaces, system integration, and testing.

Game Development

  • Roblox Studio — 3D environments, gameplay development, and multiplayer systems.
  • Luau — Resource simulation, mission logic, puzzles, and player interactions.
  • Visual Studio Code — Code editing and script organization.
  • Blender — 3D modeling and asset editing.

Development and Collaboration

  • GitHub — Version control, project files, and documentation.
  • Roblox Creator Hub — Publishing and game configuration.

AI-Assisted Development helped us save time during the hackathon, while our team led, tested, and took full responsibility.

  • Claude AI — Assistance with scripting and debugging.
  • ChatGPT — Support with visual assets and documentation.

Scientific Resources

  • NASA Open Resources — Scientific data, historical research, and educational references.

5. Design Decisions and Challenges

Our main challenge was combining scientific relevance, engaging gameplay, and accessibility within a two-day hackathon.

We focused on five considerations:

  • Scientific Relevance: Connecting NASA research to specific puzzles, environmental information, and simulation parameters.
  • Engineering Trade-offs: Designing resource systems where decisions about power, oxygen, food, and protection affect one another.
  • Accessibility: Providing clear objectives, bilingual interfaces, and guidance through NAJM for children aged 7–12.
  • Gameplay Progression: Connecting exploration, station restoration, scientific discoveries, mystery-solving, and survival into one mission.
  • Technical Integration: Developing and integrating the storyline, interactive environments, multiplayer systems, resource simulation, and mission interfaces within the hackathon period.

These decisions shaped a game that combines educational objectives with interactive gameplay.

6. Educational Benefits and Intended Impact

SADEEM aims to introduce young players to the engineering challenges of space exploration through practical decision-making.

The intended learning outcomes include:

  • Critical Thinking: Understanding how one decision can affect multiple systems.
  • Problem-Solving: Completing scientific tasks, interpreting clues, and solving puzzles.
  • Resource Management: Balancing limited power, oxygen, food, and protection.
  • Scientific Understanding: Exploring lunar and Martian environmental conditions using NASA research.
  • Teamwork: Coordinating decisions and objectives during cooperative gameplay.
  • STEM Curiosity: Developing an interest in space science, technology, and engineering.

The game also introduces Saudi astronaut representation within a fictional future mission, helping connect space exploration with the interests and aspirations of young learners in Saudi Arabia.

Beyond memorizing scientific facts, SADEEM encourages players to understand how engineering decisions influence mission outcomes.

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of explorers by letting them experience the challenges of surviving beyond Earth.
